sql:
SELECT z.LocationID, z.Borough, z.Zone, COUNT(t.PULocationID) AS cash_trips
FROM ops.zones z
LEFT JOIN lake.trips t ON t.PULocationID = z.LocationID AND t.payment_type = 2
GROUP BY z.LocationID, z.Borough, z.Zone
ORDER BY z.LocationID

diagnosis.bottleneck: The query scans the entire trips table (495K rows) to filter payment_type=2, then performs a hash join with a CAST on the join key, and finally aggregates ~99K rows; the sequential scan and the cast in the join condition are the primary cost drivers.

plan_nodes.note: Join Type: RIGHT | Conditions: CAST(PULocationID AS BIGINT) = LocationID | Estimated Cardinality: 99167

hypotheses.claim: A filter on the joined side sits in the ON clause of a LEFT JOIN; the join dominates the cost. (matched: left join lake.trips t on … and t.payment_type = 2)

The CAST(PULocationID AS BIGINT) in the join condition forces per-row type conversion during hash join probing, increasing CPU; if PULocationID and LocationID share a compatible integer type, removing the cast could eliminate this overhead.

The RIGHT HASH JOIN builds the hash table on the small zones table (265 rows) but probes with 99K trips rows; the join's output cardinality equals the filtered trips count, indicating no early aggregation—pre-aggregating trips by PULocationID before the join could reduce probe volume.
